chunk-001:c007.proposition: Science does not establish that all reality began from nothing, and exempting God from causal explanation equally permits an uncaused universe.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Natural selection, fossils, and genetic commonality explain apparent biological design without requiring inference to a divine designer.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Extensive undeserved natural and animal suffering conflicts with an omniscient, omnipotent, and wholly good creator, while unguided evolution offers an alternative account.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Late and religiously interested testimony is too slender to justify a resurrection claim that conflicts with established natural regularities.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Evolution can account for consciousness and elementary truth-directed rational capacities, so naturalism need not undermine confidence in human reasoning.

chunk-003:c003-01.proposition: Appeals to divine participation, resurrection, and future compensation neither explain the distribution of suffering nor compensate the nonhuman animals excluded from standard Christian afterlife hope.

chunk-003:c003-03.proposition: Finite personal and social hopes remain possible without immortality, while the psychological attractiveness of an afterlife does not supply evidence that it exists.

chunk-003:c003-06.proposition: Objective moral conclusions can be rationally defended without God by impartially recognizing that one's interests do not automatically outweigh comparable interests and suffering experienced by others.

chunk-003:c003-07.proposition: Human origins admit an evolutionary explanation, and individuals can create purposes for their finite lives without an ultimate purpose bestowed by an external source.

chunk-003:c003-09.proposition: Failed expectations, factual unreliability, and morally objectionable scriptural passages weaken biblical authority and prevent its portrait of Jesus from adequately establishing his divinity.
